study: Cabell et al. (2011), teacher responsivity-education PD (adapted Hanen/LLLI), pre-K, Am. J. Speech-Lang. Pathology
eval_evidence: Authored/conducted by the team that developed/adapted the responsivity-education program ('as part of our intervention, we included content...'); IES grant R305F05124. Developer-conducted RCT, no independent evaluator.
developer_evidence: Delivered by the research team's own staff: SLP/facilitators led the group workshops (one facilitator per session Hanen-certified) and 'classroom teachers ... were assigned to a trained research assistant serving as a consultant' for the distance coaching.
cascade_evidence: Research-team facilitators/RAs trained and coached the teachers directly; no train-the-trainer or lead-teacher tier (teachers do not re-deliver to others).
counterfactual_evidence: Control was an explicit 'business-as-usual' condition; control teachers 'engaged in business-as-usual practices' and were not supported in any way. No active alternative PD.
coaching_evidence: Reduced-intensity model: a fall and winter workshop plus DISTANCE coaching (the paper explicitly studies 'reduced intensity training and distance coaching'). Periodic remote coaching with video feedback rather than frequent recurring in-person in-class cycles.
student_dose_evidence: Intervention changes teacher conversational/responsivity practices; no tutoring, pull-out, or student-facing software dose added beyond regular instruction.
maturity_evidence: Single academic-year implementation (fall/winter workshops, spring outcomes); program designed as a one-year PD with no second-year/teacher-experience maturity axis.
